attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'nothing like a robust response' as a claim that no robust defense exists. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: robust means broadly reliable against varied realistic attacks, not perfect, and existing mitigations are allowed. Using Jul-Sep 2024 as the period is reasonable for an ongoing observation.

evidence.note: Independent preprint posted Aug/Sep 2024, inside the target quarter. It finds that existing defenses fail to generalize to multi-turn human jailbreaks, with much higher attack success rates than automated attacks achieve.
Company disclosure from April 2024, before the quarter. It reports a mitigation for one attack type, which does not show broad robustness.

reviews.rationale: Independent evaluation inside the target quarter shows that credible defenses failed substantially under realistic multi-turn attacks, which meets the support condition. Anthropic's mitigation for one attack is the kind of narrow fix the contract excludes as contradiction.

attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own 2023 essay and reaffirms it as 'Still true', so it is his endorsed claim.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps every component and the comparative wording on text similarity versus moral calculus. It is a compound observation about ChatGPT at the time of the post.

contract.note: The readings are ordinary: outsiders lack disclosure, guardrails fail sometimes, glorified means favorable treatment. Choosing September 2024 is reasonable. Support requires every component to hold.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of Similarweb data for September 2024. It shows ChatGPT leading chatbot web visits, which supports the most-used component on that measure only.

OpenAI's own September 2024 disclosure that GPT-4o scored 22 of 100 on a hard jailbreak test, supporting incomplete guardrails. Its claim that o1 reasons about safety rules is unverified company material.
OpenAI's March 2023 report, which withholds training and dataset details. It predates the target period, so it gives background for the disclosure component only.
Independent tests from before the target period show both jailbreak successes and better GPT-4o text safety. They do not separate text similarity from moral reasoning.
Media study covering 2022-23. It finds more attention but also more framing around risk, which cautions against reading attention as glorification. Not the target period.

reviews.rationale: Usage leadership on web visits and incomplete jailbreak resistance are supported for September 2024. No evidence settles the media-glorification component or the claim that guardrails rest on text similarity rather than moral calculus. Nothing contradicts any component. The support condition needs all parts, so the compound claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence opening his post.

semantics.note: 'Going to be' is unhedged, and the antecedent (more use) is kept. 'Trouble' is vague, and the speaker gave no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'trouble' as privacy and security harm follows the post's context. Requiring realized harm rather than detected violations is fair. With no deadline, only a decisive longitudinal study could settle it early.

evidence.note: St. Louis Fed survey shows generative-AI adoption rising through August 2025. This establishes the antecedent but measures no harm.
Netskope vendor telemetry shows threefold growth in genAI users and doubled detected data-policy violations. That supports the antecedent, but detected violations are not verified realized harms.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent is met because LLM use grew. No deadline was stated, and no decisive longitudinal study links expanded use to increased realized security harm. Doubled detected policy violations do not meet the early-resolution rule. The forecast cannot yet be scored.

semantics.note: 'Asking for trouble' is a rhetorical, normative warning with no specified harm, comparison or horizon. It is not a testable causal claim.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to invent a binary condition and treats the claim as not applicable.

evidence.note: Robot-jailbreak preprint from Oct 17, 2024 shows one concrete vulnerability. It says nothing on the societal causal effect of empowering companies.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended warning with no defined outcome, measure or time window. Laboratory vulnerability results cannot support or refute it, so it is not adjudicable.
